en: Points of Controversy Great Chapter Fifteen Sixteenth Section
The Discussion on Whether Matter is a Cause:
Is matter a cause?
Yes, it is.
Is non-greed the cause?
One should not say so ... pe ...
Is non-hatred the cause? ... pe ...
Non-delusion is a cause;
greed is a cause;
hatred is a cause.
Is delusion a cause?
One should not say so … [and so on] … Is material form a cause?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Does it have an object? Is there its turning toward [the object] … pe … its aspiration?
You should not speak thus … pe …
But surely it has no object; there is for it no turning toward [the object], nor... nor aspiration? Yes, you say.
If it has no object, and there is for it no turning toward [the object], nor... nor aspiration, then indeed, sir, you should not say: [that it is consciousness].
“Form is a cause.
Is non-greed a cause that has an object, and does it possess turning toward [the object], and so forth, up to aspiration? Yes.
“Form is a cause, it has an object, there is its turning toward [it], ... pe ... and its aspiration”?
One should not say so ... pe ...
“Hatredlessness is a cause ... [and so on].
Non-delusion is a cause;
greed is a cause;
hatred is a cause.
Delusion is a cause that has an object; does it have turning toward [the object], and so forth, up to aspiration? Yes.
Is form a cause that has an object; does it have turning toward [the object], and so forth, up to aspiration?
It should not be said thus...
[as before] ...Is it the case that material form (rūpa) is a cause without an object (anārammaṇa), and that there is no turning toward it (āvaṭṭanā)... [as before] ...nor aspiration (paṇidhi)? Yes.
Is non-greed (alobha) a cause that is without an object, and for it there is no turning toward [objects], nor aspiration?
One should not say so...
Is material form (rūpa) a cause that is without an object, and for it there is no turning toward [objects], nor aspiration? One should not say so either.
Yes. Non-hatred is a cause… non-delusion is a cause…

Is greed a cause without an object, and is there no turning toward it... up to ... no aspiration? Is hatred a cause without an object, and is there no turning toward it... up to ... no aspiration? Is delusion a cause without an object, and is there no turning toward it... up to ... no aspiration?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Should it not be said that “form is a cause”?
“Yes.
“Is it not the case that the great elements are the supporting causes for derived matter?
“Yes.”
If the great elements are the supporting cause for derived matter, then indeed, O sir, it must be said:
"Matter is a cause.
The discussion on whether matter is a cause is concluded.
